brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Color-coded top borders per category create immediate visual taxonomy and a memorable spatial signature on dark canvas
Concept rejects the list/grid orthodoxy as briefed — a genuine attempt at proximity-based document organization
Tag chips, file-type labels, and tinted icon tiles show consistent micro-component language across cards
dominant_weaknesses: Cards visibly overlap and occlude category labels ('DEVELOPMENT', 'PERSONAL', 'ARCHIVE') and even card content, breaking legibility
Spatial layout feels accidental rather than meaningful — staircase cascading reads as broken grid, not topic proximity
No visible affordances for the spatial metaphor: no clustering halos, links, zoom, or grouping cues to justify the canvas
fix_priorities: Resolve overlap: enforce non-collision or use intentional stacking with z-order shadows and category labels above cards
Make proximity semantic: add soft cluster auras, connecting lines, or distance-encodes-relatedness to earn the canvas
Introduce interaction signals (drag handles, zoom/pan hint, minimap) so the spatial paradigm is discoverable
Tighten typographic hierarchy — category headers are too faint and collide with card chrome
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral pull from neon accents on black is decent, but behavioral usability collapses under overlapping cards, and reflective payoff is undermined because the spatial metaphor isn't legibly meaningful.
rationale.intent_fit: It gestures at the brief's spatial-canvas idea but executes it as a messy offset grid with no proximity semantics, so the concept remains aspirational rather than realized.
